title.zh: 卷七十六 志第五十二 職官五
title.raw: 卷七十六 志第五十二 職官五 Volume 76 Treatises 52: Official Posts 5

sentences.zh: 公侯伯駙馬都尉附儀賓五軍都督府京營京衛錦衣衛附旗手等衛南京守備南京五軍都督府南京衛王府護衛附儀衛司總兵官留守司都司附行都司各衛各所宣慰司宣撫司安撫司招討司長官司附蠻夷長官司軍民府附土州土縣

translations.literal: Dukes, Marquises, and Earls; Chief Commandants for the Imperial Son-in-Law with appended Ceremonial Guests; the Five Chief Military Commissions; the Capital Garrison; Capital Guards; the Embroidered Uniform Guard with appended Archery Guards and related guards; Nanjing Garrison Command; Nanjing Five Chief Military Commissions; Nanjing Guards; Princely Household Guards with appended Ceremonial Guard Offices; Regional Commander-in-Chief; Garrison Command; Regional Military Commission with appended traveling Regional Military Commission; each guard and battalion; Pacification Commission; Pacification Superintendent Commission; Comforting Commission; Pacification and Suppression Commission; Native Official post with appended native chieftain posts; Military-Civilian Prefecture with appended native prefecture and native subprefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes, marquises, and earls; chief commandants for imperial sons-in-law (with ceremonial guests appended); the five chief military commissions; the capital garrison; capital guards; the Embroidered Uniform Guard (with archery and related guards); Nanjing garrison command; Nanjing five chief military commissions; Nanjing guards; princely household guards (with ceremonial guard offices); regional commander-in-chief; garrison command; regional military commissions (with traveling commissions); every guard and battalion; pacification commissions; pacification superintendent commissions; comforting commissions; pacification and suppression commissions; native official posts (with native chieftain posts); military-civilian prefectures (with native prefectures and subprefectures).

sentences.zh: 公、侯、伯，凡三等，以封功臣及外戚，皆有流有世。

translations.literal: Dukes, marquises, and earls—three ranks in all—were conferred upon meritorious ministers and imperial affines; some titles were non-hereditary and some hereditary.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes, marquises, and earls formed three ranks, conferred on meritorious ministers and imperial relatives by marriage; titles could be either non-hereditary or hereditary.

sentences.zh: 功臣則給鐵券，封號四等：佐太祖定天下者，曰開國輔運推誠；

translations.literal: Meritorious ministers were granted iron certificates; ennoblement titles fell into four grades: those who assisted the founding emperor in pacifying the realm were styled "Loyal in Founding the State, Aiding the Mandate, and Advancing Sincerity";
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious ministers received iron certificates. There were four grades of ennoblement title: those who had aided the founding emperor in establishing the realm were styled "Loyal in Founding the State, Aiding the Mandate, and Advancing Sincerity";

sentences.zh: 從成祖起兵，曰奉天靖難推誠；

translations.literal: those who followed the Yongle Emperor in raising troops were styled "Loyal to Heaven in Pacifying Disorder and Advancing Sincerity";
translations.idiomatic: those who had followed the Yongle Emperor in raising troops were styled "Loyal to Heaven in Pacifying Disorder and Advancing Sincerity";

sentences.zh: 餘曰奉天翊運推誠，曰奉天翊衛推誠。

translations.literal: the remainder were styled "Loyal to Heaven in Supporting the Mandate and Advancing Sincerity" or "Loyal to Heaven in Supporting the Guard and Advancing Sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: all others were styled either "Loyal to Heaven in Supporting the Mandate and Advancing Sincerity" or "Loyal to Heaven in Supporting the Guard and Advancing Sincerity."

sentences.zh: 武臣曰宣力武臣，文臣曰守正文臣。

translations.literal: Military ministers were styled "Military Ministers Who Proclaim Their Strength"; civil ministers were styled "Civil Ministers Who Uphold Correctness."
translations.idiomatic: For military ministers the epithet was "minister who proclaims his strength"; for civil ministers, "minister who upholds correctness."

sentences.zh: 歲祿以功為差。

translations.literal: Annual stipends varied according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: Annual stipends were graded according to merit.

sentences.zh: 已封而又有功，仍爵或進爵，增祿。

translations.literal: If one already ennobled rendered further merit, he might retain his title or be advanced in rank, with increased stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Those already ennobled who rendered further service might retain their title or be promoted, with increased stipends.

sentences.zh: 其才而賢者，充京營總督，五軍都督府掌僉書，南京守備，或出充鎮守總兵官，否則食祿奉朝請而已。

translations.literal: Those of talent and virtue might serve as superintendent of the Capital Garrison, chief secretary of a Five Armies Commission, Nanjing garrison command, or be sent out as regional commander-in-chief on garrison duty; otherwise they merely drew stipends and attended court as honorary officials.
translations.idiomatic: Men of talent and character might be appointed superintendent of the capital garrison, chief secretary in a Five Armies Commission, Nanjing garrison commander, or dispatched as regional commander-in-chief; otherwise they merely received stipends and attended court as honorary officials.

sentences.zh: 年幼而嗣爵者，鹹入國子監讀書。

translations.literal: Those who succeeded to a title while young all entered the Directorate of Education to study.
translations.idiomatic: Heirs who succeeded while still young were all sent to study at the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年，定外戚封爵毋許世襲，其有世襲一二代者，出特恩。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiajing it was fixed that ennoblement of imperial affines by marriage must not be hereditary; where hereditary descent for one or two generations was granted, it came by special favor.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 8 (1529) it was decreed that titles granted to imperial affines by marriage must not pass by hereditary succession; where one or two generations of inheritance were allowed, that was a special grace.

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉，位在伯上。

translations.literal: The Chief Commandant for the Imperial Son-in-Law ranked above an earl.
translations.idiomatic: The chief commandant for an imperial son-in-law ranked above an earl.

sentences.zh: 凡尚大長公主、長公主、公主，並曰駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: All who married the emperor's senior paternal aunt, paternal aunt, or daughter were styled Chief Commandant for the Imperial Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever married the emperor's senior paternal aunt, paternal aunt, or daughter received the title chief commandant for the imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 其尚郡主、縣主、郡君、縣君、鄉君者，並曰儀賓。

translations.literal: Those who married a commandery princess, county princess, commandery lady, county lady, or township lady were all styled Ceremonial Guest.
translations.idiomatic: Marriages to a commandery princess, county princess, or the lesser noble ladies of commandery, county, or township rank conferred the title ceremonial guest.

sentences.zh: 歲祿各有差，皆不得與政事。

translations.literal: Annual stipends each had fixed grades; none might take part in government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Annual stipends varied by rank, and none of these men might participate in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 明初，駙馬都尉有典兵出鎮及掌府部事者。

translations.literal: In early Ming, chief commandants for imperial sons-in-law sometimes commanded troops on garrison duty or headed ministry and commission offices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty, some chief commandants for imperial sons-in-law commanded armies on garrison duty or headed ministry offices.

sentences.zh: 建文時，梅殷為鎮守淮安總兵官，李堅為左副將軍。

translations.literal: Under the Jianwen reign, Mei Yin served as regional commander-in-chief garrisoning Huai'an, and Li Jian as left deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Jianwen, Mei Yin was regional commander-in-chief at Huai'an and Li Jian left deputy general.

sentences.zh: 成祖時，李讓掌北京行部事。

translations.literal: Under the Yongle Emperor, Li Rang directed the Beijing traveling ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yongle Emperor, Li Rang directed the traveling ministry at Beijing.

sentences.zh: 仁宗時沐昕，宣宗時宋琥，並守備南京。

translations.literal: Under the Hongxi Emperor, Mu Xin; under the Xuande Emperor, Song Hu—all served as Nanjing garrison commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongxi, Mu Xin; under Xuande, Song Hu—both held Nanjing garrison command.

sentences.zh: 英宗時，趙輝掌南京左府事。

translations.literal: Under the Zhengtong Emperor, Zhao Hui directed the left office of the Nanjing ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengtong, Zhao Hui directed the left office of the Nanjing ministry.

sentences.zh: 其餘惟奉祀孝陵，攝行廟祭，署宗人府事。

translations.literal: Otherwise their duties were limited to offering sacrifice at the Xiaoling mausoleum, presiding over temple rites, and acting in the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise they only offered sacrifice at the Xiaoling mausoleum, presided over temple rites, or acted in the Court of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 往往受命，一充其任。

translations.literal: When appointed, they generally fulfilled that single charge.
translations.idiomatic: When given an appointment, they usually discharged that one duty alone.

sentences.zh: 若恩親侯李貞，永春侯王甯，京山侯崔元，以恩澤封侯，非制也。

translations.literal: Cases such as the Marquis of Enqin Li Zhen, the Marquis of Yongchun Wang Ning, and the Marquis of Jingshan Cui Yuan—ennobled as marquises through grace rather than merit—were contrary to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffments such as Li Zhen as Marquis of Enqin, Wang Ning as Marquis of Yongchun, and Cui Yuan as Marquis of Jingshan—marquisates granted through favor rather than merit—were irregular.

sentences.zh: 中軍、左軍、右軍、前軍、後軍五都督府，每府左、右都督，正一品都督同知，從一品都督僉事，正二品，恩功寄祿，無定員。

translations.literal: The Five Chief Military Commissions—Central, Left, Right, Forward, and Rear—each had left and right commanders-in-chief of the first rank, vice commanders-in-chief of the second rank, and assistant commanders-in-chief of the third rank; posts granted by grace for merit carried stipends but had no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: The five commissions—Central, Left, Right, Forward, and Rear—each had left and right commanders-in-chief (first rank), vice commanders-in-chief (second rank), and assistant commanders-in-chief (third rank); grace and merit appointments carried stipends but had no fixed establishment.

sentences.zh: 其屬，經歷司，經歷，從五品都事，從七品各一人。

translations.literal: Their subordinates: a Registry with one Registrar of the fifth rank and one Secretary of the seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate to each commission was a Registry: one Registrar (fifth rank) and one Secretary (seventh rank).

sentences.zh: 都督府掌軍旅之事，各領其都司、衛所，詳見《兵志·衛所》中以達於兵部。

translations.literal: The commissions directed military affairs, each overseeing its regional military commissions and guards and battalions, as detailed in the Treatise on Military Affairs under Guards and Battalions, reporting upward to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: The commissions managed military affairs, each overseeing its regional commissions, guards, and battalions (see the Treatise on Military Affairs, "Guards and Battalions") and reporting to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 凡武職，世官流官、土官襲替、優養、優給，所屬上之府，移兵部請選。

translations.literal: For all military offices—hereditary posts, appointive posts, succession among native officials, preferential maintenance and grants—the subordinate office reported to its commission, which forwarded the matter to the Ministry of War to request selection.
translations.idiomatic: For every military post—hereditary, appointive, native succession, preferential maintenance or grants—the subordinate office reported to its commission, which referred the matter to the Ministry of War for selection.

sentences.zh: 既選，移府，以下之都司、衛所。

translations.literal: Once selection was made, the commission forwarded the appointment down to the regional military commissions, guards, and battalions.
translations.idiomatic: After selection, the commission notified the regional commissions, guards, and battalions below.

sentences.zh: 首領官聽吏部選授，給由亦如之。

translations.literal: Chief posts were appointed by the Ministry of Personnel on nomination; patent documents were issued in the same manner.
translations.idiomatic: Head officers were appointed on nomination by the Ministry of Personnel, with patents issued accordingly.

sentences.zh: 凡武官誥敕、俸糧、水陸步騎操練、官舍旗役並試、軍情聲息、軍伍勾補、邊腹地圖、文冊、屯種、器械、舟車、薪葦之事，並移所司而綜理之。

translations.literal: All matters of military patents and edicts, stipends and grain rations, training of infantry and cavalry on land and water, housing and banner service including examinations, military intelligence, muster and replacement of troops, frontier maps, documents, garrison farming, weapons, boats and carts, and fuel and reed supplies were referred to the responsible offices and coordinated by the commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Patents and edicts, pay and rations, land and naval drill, quarters and banner service (including examinations), intelligence, musters and replacements, frontier maps and registers, garrison agriculture, arms, transport, and fuel—all were routed through the appropriate offices and coordinated by the commissions.

sentences.zh: 凡各省、各鎮鎮守總兵官，副總兵，並以三等真、署都督及公、侯、伯充之。

translations.literal: Regional commanders-in-chief and deputy commanders-in-chief in every province and garrison circuit were filled by substantive or acting commanders of the three grades and by dukes, marquises, or earls.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial and circuit regional commanders-in-chief and their deputies were normally filled by substantive or acting commanders of the three grades, or by dukes, marquises, and earls.

sentences.zh: 有大徵討，則掛諸號將軍或大將軍、前將軍、副將軍印總兵出，既事，納之。

translations.literal: For major campaigns, they bore seals styled General, Grand General, Forward General, or Deputy General and took the field; when the affair ended, the seals were returned.
translations.idiomatic: On major campaigns they were given seals bearing titles such as General, Grand General, Forward General, or Deputy General and took command in the field; when the campaign ended, the seals were surrendered.

sentences.zh: 其各府之掌印及僉書，率皆公、侯、伯。

translations.literal: The seal-holders and chief secretaries in each commission were almost always dukes, marquises, or earls.
translations.idiomatic: The men who held the commission seals and served as chief secretaries were almost always dukes, marquises, or earls.

sentences.zh: 間有屬老將之實為都督者，不能十一也。

translations.literal: Occasionally a veteran who actually held the rank of commander-in-chief was appointed; such cases did not amount to one in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Only occasionally was a veteran who actually held the rank of commander-in-chief appointed—fewer than one in ten.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖下集慶，即置行樞密院，自領之。

translations.literal: At first, when the founding emperor took Jiqing, he established a traveling Bureau of Military Affairs and directed it himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor first took Jiqing, he established a traveling Bureau of Military Affairs and directed it personally.

sentences.zh: 又置諸翼統軍元帥府。

translations.literal: He also established Generalissimo's Headquarters for the various wings.
translations.idiomatic: He also set up generalissimo headquarters for the various wings.

sentences.zh: 尋罷樞密院，改置大都督府。

translations.literal: Soon the Bureau of Military Affairs was abolished and replaced by the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau was soon abolished and replaced by the Chief Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 以硃文正為大都督，節制中外諸軍事，設司馬、參軍、經歷、都事等官。

translations.literal: Zhu Wenzheng was made chief commander, with authority over all military affairs within and without; posts of marshal, staff officer, registrar, and secretary were established.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wenzheng became chief commander with authority over all military affairs; marshals, staff officers, registrars, and secretaries were appointed.

sentences.zh: 又增設左、右都督，同知，副使，僉事，照磨各一人，並設斷事官。

translations.literal: Left and right commanders-in-chief, vice commanders, assistant commanders, registrars, and secretaries were added, one of each, and judicial officers were also established.
translations.idiomatic: Left and right commanders-in-chief, vice commanders, assistant commanders, registrars, and secretaries were added (one of each), along with judicial officers.

sentences.zh: 定制，大都督從一品，左、右都督正二品，同知都督從二品，副都督正三品，僉都督從三品，經歷從五品，都事從七品；

translations.literal: By regulation the chief commander was of the second rank; left and right commanders-in-chief of the third rank; vice commanders of the fourth rank; assistant commanders of the fifth rank; registrars of the sixth rank; secretaries of the eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Regulations fixed the chief commander at second rank, left and right commanders at third rank, vice commanders at fourth, assistant commanders at fifth, registrars at sixth, and secretaries at eighth;

sentences.zh: 統軍元帥府元帥正三品，同知元帥從三品，副使正四品，經歷正七品，知事從八品，照磨正九品；

translations.literal: the generalissimo of a wing headquarters was of the third rank, vice generalissimo of the fourth, deputy of the fifth, registrar of the eighth, secretary of the ninth, and registrar-clerk of the ninth rank;
translations.idiomatic: at wing headquarters the generalissimo was third rank, vice generalissimo fourth, deputy fifth, registrar eighth, secretary ninth, and registrar-clerk ninth;

sentences.zh: 又以都鎮撫司隸大都督府，先是屬中書省秩從四品。

translations.literal: the Commission for Military Pacification was also placed under the Chief Military Commission; it had previously been subordinate to the Secretariat at the fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: the Commission for Military Pacification was placed under the Chief Military Commission, having previously been a fourth-rank office under the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋罷統軍元帥府。

translations.literal: The wing generalissimo headquarters were soon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The wing generalissimo headquarters were soon abolished.

sentences.zh: 吳元年，更定官制，罷大都督不設，以左、右都督為長官，正一品同知都督，從一品副都督，正二品僉都督，從二品俱升品秩。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Wu reign era the official system was revised: the post of chief commander was abolished and not re-established; left and right commanders-in-chief became the chief officers at the first rank, vice commanders at the second, and assistant commanders at the third—all ranks were raised.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu year 1 the system was revised: the chief commander was abolished; left and right commanders-in-chief became chiefs (first rank), vice commanders second rank, assistant commanders third—all ranks were raised.

sentences.zh: 其屬，設參議，正四品經歷，斷事官，從五品都事，正七品照磨從七品洪武九年，罷副都督，改參議為掌判官。

translations.literal: Subordinates included Counselors (fourth rank), Registrars, Judicial Officers (fifth rank), Secretaries (seventh rank), and Registrar-Clerks (seventh rank). In the ninth year of Hongwu the vice commander was abolished and Counselor was changed to Chief Adjudicator.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates were Counselors (fourth rank), Registrars, Judicial Officers (fifth rank), Secretaries (seventh rank), and Registrar-Clerks (seventh rank). In Hongwu 9 the vice commander was abolished and Counselor became Chief Adjudicator.

sentences.zh: 十二年，升都督僉事為正二品，掌判官為正三品。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, assistant commanders were raised to the second rank and chief adjudicators to the third.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 12 assistant commanders were raised to second rank and chief adjudicators to third.

sentences.zh: 十三年，始改都督府為五軍都督府，分領在京各衛所，惟錦衣等親軍，上直衛不隸五府。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Chief Military Commission became the Five Chief Military Commissions, each overseeing capital guards and battalions; the Embroidered Uniform Guard and other personal guards and the imperial guard were not subordinate to the five commissions.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 13 the commission became five commissions, each overseeing capital guards and battalions; the Embroidered Uniform Guard, personal guards, and imperial guard were excluded.

sentences.zh: 及在外各都司、衛所，以中軍都督府斷事官為五軍斷事官。

translations.literal: For regional military commissions, guards, and battalions outside the capital, the judicial officer of the Central Commission served as judicial officer for all five.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the capital, the Central Commission's judicial officer served as judicial officer for all five commissions.

sentences.zh: 十五年，置五軍十衛參軍府，設左、右參軍。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the Five Armies Ten Guards Staff Office was established with left and right staff officers.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 15 the Five Armies Ten Guards Staff Office was set up with left and right staff officers.

sentences.zh: 十七年，五軍各設左、右斷事二人，提控案牘一人，並從九品二十三年，升五軍斷事官為正五品，總治五軍刑獄。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year each of the five armies appointed two left and right judicial officers and one records controller, all of the ninth rank. In the twenty-third year the Five Armies judicial officers were raised to the fifth rank to oversee military justice in all five armies.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 17 each army appointed two left and right judicial officers and one records controller (ninth rank). In Hongwu 23 the Five Armies judicial officers were raised to fifth rank to oversee military justice.

sentences.zh: 分為五司，司設稽仁、稽義、稽禮、稽智、稽信五人，俱正七品，各理其軍之刑獄。

translations.literal: They were divided into five offices; each office had five officers—Investigating Humanity, Righteousness, Rites, Wisdom, and Trustworthiness—of the seventh rank, each handling that army's criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: Five offices were created, each with five seventh-rank officers—Investigating Humanity, Righteousness, Rites, Wisdom, and Trustworthiness—who handled that army's cases.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，置五軍照磨所，專掌文牘。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year the Five Armies Registry Office was established to manage documents exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 29 the Five Armies Registry Office was established solely to manage documents.

sentences.zh: 建文中，革斷事及五司官。

translations.literal: Under the Jianwen reign the judicial officers and the five offices were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianwen the judicial officers and five offices were abolished.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年，設北京留守行後軍都督府，置左、右都督，都督同知，都督僉事，無定員，經歷、都事各一人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle the Beijing Rear Garrison Traveling Chief Military Commission was established, with left and right commanders-in-chief, vice commanders, and assistant commanders without fixed quota, and one registrar and one secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 1 the Beijing Rear Garrison traveling commission was established with left and right commanders, vice and assistant commanders (no fixed quota), one registrar, and one secretary.

sentences.zh: 後又分五府，稱行在五軍都督府。

translations.literal: Later it was divided into five commissions, called the Traveling Five Chief Military Commissions.
translations.idiomatic: It was later split into five commissions called the Traveling Five Chief Military Commissions.

sentences.zh: 十八年，除「行在。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, the designation "Traveling [at court]" was removed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 the designation "Traveling [at court]" was dropped.

sentences.zh: 」字，在應天者加「南京。

translations.literal: " For those at Yingtian, "Nanjing" was added.
translations.idiomatic: For offices at Yingtian, the prefix "Nanjing" was added.
(closing the designation.)

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年，復稱行在，仍設行後府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi the title "Traveling" was restored and the traveling rear commission re-established.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongxi 1 the "Traveling" designation was restored and the traveling rear commission re-established.

sentences.zh: 宣德三年又革。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuande it was abolished again.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 3 it was abolished again.

sentences.zh: 正統六年，復除「行在。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengtong, the designation "Traveling [at court]" was again removed.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 6 the "Traveling [at court]" designation was removed again.
(closing the designation.)

sentences.zh: 京營，永樂二十二年，置三大營，曰五軍營，曰神機營，曰三千營。

translations.literal: The Capital Garrison: in the twenty-second year of Yongle three great camps were established—the Five Armies Camp, the Divine Engine Camp, and the Three Thousand Camp.
translations.idiomatic: The capital garrison: in Yongle 22 three great camps were created—the Five Armies Camp, Divine Engine Camp, and Three Thousand Camp.

sentences.zh: 五軍、神機各設中軍、左右哨、左右掖；

translations.literal: The Five Armies and Divine Engine camps each had a central army and left and right vanguard, left and right flank, and left and right rear divisions;
translations.idiomatic: The Five Armies and Divine Engine camps each had a central army plus left and right vanguard, flank, and rear divisions;

sentences.zh: 五軍、三千各設五司。

translations.literal: the Five Armies and Three Thousand camps each had five offices.
translations.idiomatic: the Five Armies and Three Thousand camps each had five administrative offices.

sentences.zh: 每營俱選勳臣二人提督之。

translations.idiomatic: Each camp was supervised by two meritorious ministers appointed as superintendents.

sentences.zh: 其諸營管哨、掖官，曰坐營，曰坐司。

translations.idiomatic: Officers over camps and their vanguard and flank units were called camp superintendent and office superintendent.

sentences.zh: 各哨、掖官，亦率以勳臣為之。

translations.literal: Officers of each vanguard and flank division were also usually meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Vanguard and flank officers were likewise usually drawn from meritorious ministers.

sentences.zh: 又設把總、把司、把牌等官。

translations.literal: Posts of company commander, office commander, and placard officer were also established.
translations.idiomatic: Company commanders, office commanders, and placard officers were also appointed.

sentences.zh: 又有圍子手、幼官、舍人、殫忠、效義諸營，俱附五軍營中。

translations.literal: There were also the Huntsmen, Junior Officers, Retainers, Devoted Loyalty, and Effective Righteousness camps, all attached to the Five Armies Camp.
translations.idiomatic: Additional camps—Huntsmen, Junior Officers, Retainers, Devoted Loyalty, and Effective Righteousness—were all attached to the Five Armies Camp.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年選三營精銳立十團營，蒞以總兵，統以總督，監以內臣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai elite troops from the three camps were chosen to form the Ten Regiment Camps, overseen by a regional commander, directed by a superintendent, and supervised by a eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 1 picked elites from the three camps formed the Ten Regiment Camps, under a regional commander, a superintendent, and a supervising eunuch.

sentences.zh: 其舊設者，號為老營。

translations.literal: The original establishments were called the Old Camps.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier organization was termed the Old Camps.

sentences.zh: 三老營凡六提督，內選其二領團營。

translations.literal: The three Old Camps had six superintendents in all; two of them were chosen to lead the Regiment Camps.
translations.idiomatic: The three Old Camps had six superintendents; two of them also commanded the Regiment Camps.

sentences.zh: 成化三年，分團營為十二，每營又各分五軍、三千統騎兵，神機統火器。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chenghua the Regiment Camps were divided into twelve; each camp was further split, with the Five Armies and Three Thousand commanding cavalry and the Divine Engine commanding firearms.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 3 the Regiment Camps became twelve; each was subdivided—the Five Armies and Three Thousand overseeing cavalry, the Divine Engine firearms.

sentences.zh: 其各營統領，俱擇都督、都指揮或列爵充之，以總督統轄之。

translations.literal: The commanders of each camp were chosen from commanders-in-chief, regional commanders, or ennobled officers, all under a superintendent's unified command.

sentences.zh: 正德中，又選團營精銳，置東西兩官廳，另設總兵、參將統領。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde reign elite Regiment Camp troops were again selected to form the Eastern and Western Staff Halls, with separate regional commanders and deputy generals.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde, elite regiment troops formed Eastern and Western Staff Halls with their own regional commanders and deputy generals.

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Jiajing the Regiment Camp staff halls were abolished and the three great camps restored; the Three Thousand Camp was renamed Divine Pivot, with deputy, assistant, mobile, adjutant, camp superintendent, signal chief, staff, and company and thousand-man commanders.

translations.literal: A vice minister was also appointed to assist in managing capital garrison military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One vice minister was added to assist in capital garrison military affairs.

sentences.zh: 定巡視科道官歲一代更，悉革內侍官。

translations.literal: Censorate and ministry touring inspectors were fixed to rotate yearly; all eunuch posts were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Touring censorate and ministry officials were to rotate annually, and all eunuch offices were abolished.

sentences.zh: 增設巡視主事，尋亦革。

translations.literal: Touring supervising secretaries were added, but soon abolished as well.
translations.idiomatic: Touring supervising secretaries were added but soon abolished too.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，仍以總督為提督，改協理為閱視，尋並改閱視為提督。

translations.literal: Early in the Longqing reign the governor title reverted to superintendent, assistant management became inspection, and inspection was soon changed back to superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longqing the governor became superintendent again, "assist" became "inspect," and "inspect" soon became superintendent again.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，更京營制，三營各設提督，又各設右都御史一員提督之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year the capital garrison system was revised: each of the three camps received its own superintendent, and each also had a right censor-in-chief as superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: In month 2 of year 4 the garrison was reorganized: each camp got a superintendent, each supervised by a right censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 九月，罷六提督，仍復總督戎政一人。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the six superintendents were abolished and a single governor of military affairs was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In month 9 the six superintendents were abolished and one governor of military affairs restored.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，增設協理一人，已，仍革一人。

translations.literal: Early in the Tianqi reign one assistant post was added; later one was abolished again.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianqi one assistant was added; later one assistant post was cut again.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，復增一人。

translations.literal: Early in the Chongzhen reign one was added again.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongzhen one assistant was added once more.

sentences.zh: 京衛指揮使司，指揮使一人，正三品指揮同知二人，從三品指揮僉事四人。

translations.literal: Capital Guard command offices: one commander of the third rank; two vice commanders of the third rank; four assistant commanders of the fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Each capital guard command had one commander (third rank), two vice commanders (third rank), and four assistant commanders (fourth rank).

sentences.zh: 正四品鎮撫司，鎮撫二人，從五品其屬，經歷司，經歷，從七品知事，正八品吏目，從九品倉大使、副使各一人。

translations.literal: A Pacification Office with two pacifiers of the fifth rank; subordinates included a Registry with a registrar of the seventh rank, a secretary of the eighth rank, a clerk of the ninth rank, and one granary commissioner and deputy each.
translations.idiomatic: A Pacification Office with two fifth-rank pacifiers; subordinates were a Registry (seventh-rank registrar), secretary (eighth rank), clerk (ninth rank), and one granary commissioner and deputy each.

sentences.zh: 所轄千戶所，多寡各不等。

translations.literal: Battalion offices under their jurisdiction varied in number.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate thousand-man battalions varied in number.

sentences.zh: 京衛有上直衛，有南、北京衛，品秩並同。

translations.idiomatic: Capital guards comprised imperial-attendance guards and Nanjing and Beijing guards, all of equal rank.

sentences.zh: 各有掌印，有僉書。

translations.idiomatic: Every guard had its seal-holder and chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 其以恩廕寄祿，無定員。

translations.literal: Those holding stipends by grace had no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Grace appointments carrying stipends had no fixed establishment.

sentences.zh: 凡上直衛親軍指揮使司，二十有六。

translations.literal: Imperial-attendance personal guard commands numbered twenty-six in all.
translations.idiomatic: There were twenty-six imperial-attendance personal guard commands.

translations.idiomatic: Namely the Embroidered Uniform Guard, Archery Guard, and Forward Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 是為上十二衛，洪武中置。

translations.idiomatic: They rotated as palace guards, protecting the inner precincts, and did not report to the five commissions.

sentences.zh: 其京衛隸都督府者，三十有三。

translations.idiomatic: Thirty-three capital guards were subordinate to the five commissions.

sentences.zh: 曰武功中衛，曰武功左衛，曰武功右衛，已上三衛以匠故，隸工部。

translations.literal: the Central, Left, and Right Wugong Guards—these three, being artisan guards, were subordinate to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: the Central, Left, and Right Wugong Guards—because they were artisan guards, they reported to the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 曰永清左衛，曰永清右衛，曰彭城衛，曰長陵衛，曰獻陵衛，曰景陵衛，曰裕陵衛，曰茂陵衛，曰泰陵衛，曰康陵衛，曰永陵衛，曰昭陵衛。

translations.literal: the Left and Right Yongqing Guards, Pengcheng Guard, and the mausoleum guards of Changling, Xianling, Jingling, Yuling, Maoling, Tailing, Kangling, Yongling, and Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Next were the Left and Right Yongqing Guards, Pengcheng Guard, and the mausoleum guards from Changling through Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 明初，置帳前總制親軍都指揮使司，以馮國用為都指揮使。

translations.literal: In early Ming the Command of Personal Guards before the Throne was established, with Feng Guoyong as commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty the Command of Personal Guards before the Throne was set up, with Feng Guoyong as commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 後改置金吾侍衛親軍都護府，設都護，從二品經歷，正六品知事，從七品照磨。

translations.literal: It was later changed to the Golden Crow Bodyguard Personal Guard Protectorate, with a protector of the second rank, a registrar of the sixth rank, a secretary of the seventh rank, and a registrar-clerk.
translations.idiomatic: It became the Golden Crow Bodyguard Personal Guard Protectorate, with a second-rank protector, sixth-rank registrar, seventh-rank secretary, and registrar-clerk.

sentences.zh: 從八品。

translations.literal: Registrar-clerk of the eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: The registrar-clerk was eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 又置各衛親軍指揮使司，設指揮使，正三品同知指揮使，從三品副使，正四品經歷，正七品知事，正八品照磨，正九品千戶所正千戶，正五品副千戶，從五品鎮撫、百戶。

translations.literal: Personal guard command offices were also established for each guard, with commanders of the third rank, vice commanders of the third rank, deputies of the fourth rank, registrars of the seventh rank, secretaries of the eighth rank, registrar-clerks of the ninth rank, and battalion chiefs, vice chiefs, pacifiers, and company officers of the fifth and sixth ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Each guard also had a personal guard command with third-rank commander and vice commander, fourth-rank deputy, seventh-rank registrar, eighth-rank secretary, ninth-rank registrar-clerk, and fifth- and sixth-rank battalion and company officers.

sentences.zh: 正六品因置武德、龍驤、豹韜、飛龍、威武、廣武、興武、英武、鷹揚、驍騎、神武、雄武、鳳翔、天策、振武、宣武、羽林十七衛親軍指揮使司，此設親軍衛之始。

translations.literal: Thereupon seventeen personal guard commands were established—Wude, Longxiang, Baotao, Feilong, Weiwu, Guangwu, Xingwu, Yingwu, Yingyang, Xiaoqi, Shenwu, Xiongwu, Fengxiang, Tianche, Zhenwu, Xuanwu, and Yulin—marking the beginning of personal guard establishments.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen personal guard commands were then created—Wude, Longxiang, Baotao, Feilong, Weiwu, Guangwu, Xingwu, Yingwu, Yingyang, Xiaoqi, Shenwu, Xiongwu, Fengxiang, Tianche, Zhenwu, Xuanwu, and Yulin—the origin of personal guard units.

sentences.zh: 尋罷金吾侍衛親軍都護府。

translations.literal: Soon the Golden Crow Bodyguard Personal Guard Protectorate was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Golden Crow Bodyguard Personal Guard Protectorate was soon abolished.

sentences.zh: 洪武、永樂間，增設親軍諸衛，名為上二十二衛，分掌宿衛。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu and Yongle reigns additional personal guards were established, called the Upper Twenty-Two Guards, sharing palace duty in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu and Yongle more personal guards were added as the Upper Twenty-Two Guards, sharing rotating palace duty.

sentences.zh: 而錦衣衛主巡察、緝捕、理詔獄，以都督、都指揮領之，蓋特異於諸衛焉。

translations.literal: The Embroidered Uniform Guard alone directed inspection, arrest, and imperial prison cases, led by a commander-in-chief or regional commander—distinct from all other guards.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Embroidered Uniform Guard handled inspection, arrest, and imperial prison cases under a commander or regional commander—unlike every other guard.

sentences.zh: 留守五衛，舊為都鎮撫司，總領禁衛，先屬中書省，改隸大都督府，設都鎮撫，從四品副鎮撫，從五品知事，從八品尋改宿衛鎮撫司，設宿衛鎮撫、宿衛知事。

translations.literal: The five garrison guards were formerly the Commission for Military Pacification, overseeing palace security; first subordinate to the Secretariat, then to the Chief Military Commission, with a pacification commissioner of the fourth rank, vice pacifier of the fifth rank, and secretary of the eighth rank; soon renamed the Palace Guard Pacification Office with palace pacifiers and secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: The five garrison guards began as the Commission for Military Pacification overseeing palace security—first under the Secretariat, then the Chief Military Commission—with fourth-rank commissioner, fifth-rank vice commissioner, and eighth-rank secretary; later renamed the Palace Guard Pacification Office.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，改為留守衛指揮使司，專領軍馬守禦各城門，及巡警皇城與城垣造作之事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu they became Garrison Guard commands, exclusively guarding city gates and patrolling the imperial city and city walls.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 3 they became garrison guard commands guarding city gates and patrolling the imperial city and walls.

sentences.zh: 後升為留守都衛，統轄天策、豹韜、飛熊、鷹揚、江陰、廣洋、橫海、龍江、水軍左、右十衛。

translations.literal: Later they were raised to the Garrison Command, overseeing Tianche, Baotao, Feixiong, Yingyang, Jiangyin, Guangyang, Henghai, Longjiang, and the Left and Right Naval Guards—ten guards in all.
translations.idiomatic: Later raised to the Garrison Command overseeing ten guards: Tianche, Baotao, Feixiong, Yingyang, Jiangyin, Guangyang, Henghai, Longjiang, and Left and Right Naval Guards.

sentences.zh: 八年，復為留守衛，與天策等八衛俱為親軍指揮使司，惟水軍左、右二衛為指揮使司。

translations.literal: In the eighth year they reverted to garrison guards; Tianche and seven others became personal guard commands, while only the Left and Right Naval Guards remained ordinary guard commands.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 they reverted to garrison guards; eight became personal guard commands, only the naval guards remaining ordinary commands.

sentences.zh: 並隸大都督府。

translations.literal: All were subordinate to the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: All of them reported to the Chief Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 十一年，改為留守中衛，增置留守左、右、前、後四衛，仍為親軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Central Garrison Guard was established and Left, Right, Forward, and Rear Garrison Guards were added, still as personal guards.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 the Central Garrison Guard was created and Left, Right, Forward, and Rear Garrison Guards added, still personal guards.

sentences.zh: 十三年，始分隸五都督府。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year they were divided among the five commissions.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 13 they were distributed among the five commissions.

sentences.zh: 錦衣衛，掌侍衛、緝捕、刑獄之事，恆以勳戚都督領之，恩廕寄祿無常員。

translations.literal: The Embroidered Uniform Guard managed bodyguard service, arrest, and criminal prisons, usually led by meritorious kin serving as commander-in-chief or regional commander; grace appointments had no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: The Embroidered Uniform Guard handled bodyguard duty, arrest, and prisons, usually under a meritorious kinsman as commander or regional commander; grace posts had no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 凡朝會、巡幸，則具鹵簿儀仗，率大漢將軍共一千五百七員等侍從扈行。

translations.literal: At court assemblies and imperial tours it furnished ceremonial guards and led one thousand five hundred seven Great Han generals and other attendants in escort.
translations.idiomatic: At audiences and tours it supplied ceremonial guards and led 1,507 Great Han generals and other escorts.

sentences.zh: 宿衛則分番入直。

translations.literal: For palace duty it rotated shifts on guard.
translations.idiomatic: For palace duty it rotated shifts.

sentences.zh: 朝日、夕月、耕耤、視牲，則服飛魚服，佩繡春刀，侍左右。

translations.literal: At sunrise and moonset audiences, plowing rites, and sacrificial inspections it wore flying-fish robes and embroidered spring knives at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn and dusk audiences, plowing rites, and sacrificial duties it wore flying-fish robes and spring knives at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 盜賊奸宄，街途溝洫，密緝而時省之。

translations.literal: Thieves and traitors in streets and drains were secretly investigated and regularly inspected.
translations.idiomatic: It secretly investigated criminals in streets and drains and inspected them regularly.

sentences.zh: 凡承製鞫獄錄囚勘事，偕三法司。

translations.literal: For imperial decrees, inquests, recording prisoners, and examining cases, it acted with the three judicial offices.
translations.idiomatic: For decrees, inquests, prisoner records, and trials it worked with the three judicial offices.

sentences.zh: 五軍官舍比試並槍，同兵部蒞視。

translations.literal: Comparative trials of Five Armies quarters and spear drill were overseen jointly with the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Five Armies quarters trials and spear drill were jointly overseen with the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 統所凡十有七。

translations.literal: It commanded seventeen battalion offices in all.
translations.idiomatic: It oversaw seventeen battalion offices in all.

sentences.zh: 中、左、右、前、後五所，領軍士。

translations.literal: Central, Left, Right, Forward, and Rear five offices commanded troops.
translations.idiomatic: Five offices—Central, Left, Right, Forward, and Rear—commanded troops.

sentences.zh: 五所分鑾輿、擎蓋、扇手、旌節、幡幢、班劍、斧鉞、戈戟、弓矢、馴馬十司，各領將軍校尉，以備法駕。

translations.literal: The five offices divided into ten departments for imperial carriage, canopy, fan-bearers, banners, flags, halberds, axes, spears, bows, and trained horses, each with generals and guardsmen for ceremonial equipage.
translations.idiomatic: Those five split into ten departments for carriage, canopy, fans, banners, flags, halberds, axes, spears, bows, and horses, each with officers for ceremonial equipage.

sentences.zh: 上中、上左、上右、上前、上後、中後六親軍所，分領將軍、力士、軍匠。

translations.literal: Six upper personal guard offices—Upper Central, Upper Left, Upper Right, Upper Forward, Upper Rear, and Central Rear—commanded generals, strongmen, and military artisans.
translations.idiomatic: Six upper personal guard offices commanded generals, strongmen, and military artisans.

sentences.zh: 馴象所，領象奴養象，以供朝會陳列、駕輦、馱寶之事。

translations.literal: An Elephant Training Office raised elephant keepers for court display, palanquin service, and carrying treasure.
translations.idiomatic: An Elephant Training Office raised keepers for court display, palanquins, and carrying treasure.

sentences.zh: 明初，置拱衛司，秩正七品，管領校尉，屬都督府。

translations.literal: In early Ming the Archguard Office was established at the seventh rank to command guardsmen, subordinate to the military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Early Ming established the seventh-rank Archguard Office commanding guardsmen under the military commission.

sentences.zh: 後改拱衛指揮使司，秩正三品。

translations.literal: It was later changed to the Archguard Command at the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Later it became the third-rank Archguard Command.

sentences.zh: 尋又改為都尉司。

translations.literal: Soon it was again changed to the Commandant's Office.
translations.idiomatic: It was soon renamed the Commandant's Office.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，改為親軍都尉府，管左、右、中、前、後五衛軍士，而設儀鸞司隸焉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu it became the Personal Guard Commandant's Office, commanding troops of the five guards, with the Ceremonial Guard Office subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 3 it became the Personal Guard Commandant's Office over five guards, with the Ceremonial Guard Office subordinate.

sentences.zh: 四年，定儀鸞司為正五品，設大使一人，副使二人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Ceremonial Guard Office was fixed at the fifth rank with one commissioner and two vice commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 the Ceremonial Guard Office was fixed at fifth rank with one commissioner and two vice commissioners.

sentences.zh: 十五年，罷儀鸞司，改置錦衣衛，秩從三品，其屬有禦椅等七員，皆正六品。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the Ceremonial Guard Office was abolished and the Embroidered Uniform Guard established at the third rank, with seven chair attendants of the sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 15 the Ceremonial Guard Office was abolished and the Embroidered Uniform Guard created at third rank with seven sixth-rank chair attendants.

sentences.zh: 設經歷司，掌文移出入；

translations.literal: A Registry managed incoming and outgoing documents;
translations.idiomatic: A Registry handled documents in and out;

sentences.zh: 鎮撫司，掌本衛刑名，兼理軍匠。

translations.literal: a Pacification Office handled the guard's criminal cases and also managed military artisans.
translations.idiomatic: a Pacification Office handled the guard's criminal cases and military artisans.

sentences.zh: 十七年，改錦衣衛指揮使為正三品。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the Embroidered Uniform Guard commander was fixed at the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 17 the guard commander was fixed at third rank.

sentences.zh: 二十年，以治錦衣衛者多非法淩虐，乃焚刑具，出繫囚，送刑部審錄，詔內外獄鹹歸三法司，罷錦衣獄。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, because many who ran the guard acted illegally and abused prisoners, torture instruments were burned, prisoners in custody were sent to the Ministry of Justice for review, and an edict ordered all prisons inside and outside to revert to the three judicial offices; the Embroidered Uniform prison was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 20, because guard officials often abused prisoners, torture gear was burned, prisoners were sent to the Ministry of Justice, all prisons were ordered back to the three judicial offices, and the guard prison was abolished.

sentences.zh: 成祖時復置。

translations.literal: Under the Yongle Emperor it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor restored it.

sentences.zh: 尋增北鎮撫司，專治詔獄。

translations.literal: Soon the Northern Pacification Office was added to handle imperial prison cases exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a Northern Pacification Office was added solely for imperial prison cases.

sentences.zh: 成化間，刻印畀之，獄成得專達，不關白錦衣，錦衣官亦不得干預。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua reign seals were engraved and given to it; once a case was closed it could report directly without informing the guard, and guard officers could not intervene.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chenghua seals were issued so closed cases could be reported directly without the guard, which could not intervene.

sentences.zh: 而以舊所設為南鎮撫司，專理軍匠。

translations.literal: The former office became the Southern Pacification Office, handling military artisans only.
translations.idiomatic: The old office became the Southern Pacification Office for military artisans only.

sentences.zh: 旗手衛，本旗手千戶所，洪武十八年改置。

translations.literal: The Archery Guard was originally the Archery Battalion; it was changed to a guard in the eighteenth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: The Archery Guard began as the Archery Battalion, made a guard in Hongwu 18.

sentences.zh: 掌大駕金鼓、旗纛，帥力士隨駕宿衛。

translations.literal: It managed great ceremonial drums, banners, and flags, leading strongmen on rotating palace guard with the imperial procession.
translations.idiomatic: It managed great ceremonial drums, banners, and flags, leading strongmen on rotating palace guard with the procession.

sentences.zh: 校尉、力士，僉民間壯丁為之。

translations.literal: Guardsmen and strongmen were recruited from sturdy commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Guardsmen and strongmen were drafted from sturdy commoners.

sentences.zh: 校尉專職擎執鹵簿儀杖，及駕前宣召官員，差遣幹辦，隸錦衣衛。

translations.literal: Guardsmen exclusively bore ceremonial regalia and summoned officials before the imperial carriage, ran errands, and were subordinate to the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Guardsmen bore ceremonial regalia, summoned officials before the carriage, ran errands, and reported to the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 力士專領金鼓、旗幟，隨駕出入，及守衛四門，隸旗手衛。

translations.literal: Strongmen exclusively managed golden drums and banners, accompanied the imperial procession, and guarded the four gates, subordinate to the Archery Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Strongmen handled drums and banners on imperial outings, guarded the four gates, and reported to the Archery Guard.

sentences.zh: 凡歲祭旗頭六纛之神，八月於壇，十二月於承天門外，皆衛官蒞事，統所五。

translations.literal: Each year at the altar in the eighth month and outside Chengtian Gate in the twelfth month they officiated at sacrifice to the Six Banners Spirit; they commanded five battalion offices.
translations.idiomatic: They officiated annually at sacrifices to the Six Banners Spirit (eighth month at the altar, twelfth month outside Chengtian Gate) and commanded five battalion offices.

sentences.zh: 府軍前衛，掌統領幼軍，輪番帶刀侍衛。

translations.literal: The Forward Military Household Guard commanded juvenile troops who rotated bearing swords on palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Forward Military Household Guard led juvenile troops who rotated with swords on palace duty.

sentences.zh: 明初，有帶刀舍人。

translations.literal: In early Ming there were sword-bearing attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Early Ming had sword-bearing attendants.

sentences.zh: 洪武時，府軍等衛皆有習技幼軍。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu era the Military Household and other guards all had juvenile troops trained in skills.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu the Military Household and other guards all trained juvenile troops in martial skills.

sentences.zh: 永樂十三年，為皇太孫特選幼軍，置府軍前衛，設官屬，指揮使五人，指揮同知十人，指揮僉事二十人，衛鎮撫十人，經歷五人。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongle juvenile troops were specially chosen for the heir apparent, the Forward Military Household Guard was established with officials: five commanders, ten vice commanders, twenty assistant commanders, and ten guard pacifiers and five registrars.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 13 juvenile troops were chosen for the heir apparent and the Forward Military Household Guard was created with five commanders, ten vice commanders, twenty assistant commanders, ten guard pacifiers, and five registrars.

sentences.zh: 統所二十有五。

translations.literal: It commanded twenty-five battalion offices.
translations.idiomatic: It oversaw twenty-five battalion offices in all.

sentences.zh: 金吾、羽林等十九衛，掌守衛巡警，統所凡一百有二。

translations.literal: The nineteen guards such as Golden Crow and Feathered Forest handled guard patrol, commanding one hundred two battalion offices in all.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteen guards including Golden Crow and Feathered Forest handled patrol duty over 102 battalion offices.

sentences.zh: 騰驤等四衛，掌帥力士直駕、隨駕，統所三十有二。

translations.literal: The four Soaring Dragon and Martial Dragon guards commanded strongmen for direct and escort duty with the emperor, commanding thirty-two battalion offices.
translations.idiomatic: The four Soaring Dragon and Martial Dragon guards led strongmen on direct and escort duty, commanding 32 battalion offices.

sentences.zh: 南京五軍都督府，左、右都督，都督同知，都督僉事，不全設。

translations.literal: The Nanjing Five Chief Military Commissions had left and right commanders-in-chief, vice commanders, and assistant commanders—not all posts filled.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing's five commissions had left and right commanders, vice commanders, and assistants—not always fully staffed.

sentences.zh: 其掌印、僉書，皆以勳爵及三等都督為之。

translations.literal: Seal-holders and chief secretaries were all filled by ennobled meritorious ministers and commanders of the three grades.
translations.idiomatic: Seal-holders and chief secretaries were drawn from ennobled merit holders and third-grade commanders.

sentences.zh: 分掌南京衛所，以達於南京兵部。

translations.literal: They oversaw Nanjing guards and battalions, reporting to the Nanjing Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: They managed Nanjing guards and battalions and reported to the Nanjing Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 凡管領大教場及江上操備等事，各府奉敕分掌之。

translations.literal: Matters such as the great drill ground and river defense preparations were each handled on imperial order by the respective commissions.
translations.idiomatic: The great drill ground and river defense were divided among the commissions by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 城門之管鑰，中府專掌之。

translations.literal: Keys to the city gates were exclusively held by the Central Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Commission alone held the city gate keys.

sentences.zh: 初設城門郎，洪武十八年革，以門禁鎖鑰銅牌，命中軍都督府掌之。

translations.literal: Gate officers were first established but abolished in the eighteenth year of Hongwu; gate locks and bronze tokens were thereafter held by the Central Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Gate officers were abolished in Hongwu 18; gate locks and bronze tokens went to the Central Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 其屬，經歷、都事各一人。

translations.literal: Subordinates: one registrar and one secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates were one registrar and one secretary.

sentences.zh: 南京衛指揮使司，設官詳京衛凡四十有九。

translations.literal: Nanjing guard commands numbered forty-nine in all, with offices as detailed for capital guards.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing had forty-nine guard commands, organized like capital guards.

sentences.zh: 分隸五都督府者三十有二。

translations.literal: Thirty-two were subordinate to the five commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-two reported to the five commissions.

sentences.zh: 曰留守左衛，曰鎮南衛，曰水軍左衛，曰驍騎右衛，曰龍虎衛，曰龍虎左衛，曰英武衛，曰龍江右衛，曰瀋陽左衛，曰瀋陽右衛，隸左府。

translations.literal: the Left Garrison Guard, Zhennan Guard, Left Naval Guard, Right Valiant Cavalry Guard, Dragon-Tiger Guard, Left Dragon-Tiger Guard, Yingwu Guard, Right Longjiang Guard, Left and Right Shenyang Guards—subordinate to the Left Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Left Commission: Left Garrison, Zhennan, Left Naval, Right Valiant Cavalry, Dragon-Tiger, Left Dragon-Tiger, Yingwu, Right Longjiang, and Left and Right Shenyang Guards.

sentences.zh: 曰留守右衛，曰虎賁右衛，曰水軍右衛，曰武德衛，曰廣武衛，隸右府。

translations.literal: the Right Garrison Guard, Right Tiger Guard, Right Naval Guard, Wude Guard, and Guangwu Guard—subordinate to the Right Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Right Commission: Right Garrison, Right Tiger, Right Naval, Wude, and Guangwu Guards.

sentences.zh: 曰留守中衛，曰神策衛，曰廣洋衛，曰廣天衛，曰和陽衛，及牧馬千戶所，隸中府。

translations.literal: the Central Garrison Guard, Shence Guard, Guangyang Guard, Guangtian Guard, Heyang Guard, and Horse Pasture battalion—subordinate to the Central Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Central Commission: Central Garrison, Shence, Guangyang, Guangtian, Heyang Guards, and Horse Pasture battalion.

sentences.zh: 曰留守前衛，曰龍江左衛，曰龍驤衛，曰飛熊衛，曰天策衛，曰豹韜衛，曰豹韜左衛，隸前府。

translations.literal: the Forward Garrison Guard, Left Longjiang Guard, Longxiang Guard, Feixiong Guard, Tianche Guard, Baotao Guard, and Left Baotao Guard—subordinate to the Forward Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Forward Commission: Forward Garrison, Left Longjiang, Longxiang, Feixiong, Tianche, Baotao, and Left Baotao Guards.

sentences.zh: 曰留守後衛，曰橫海衛，曰鷹揚衛，曰興武衛，曰江陰衛，隸後府。

translations.literal: the Rear Garrison Guard, Henghai Guard, Yingyang Guard, Xingwu Guard, and Jiangyin Guard—subordinate to the Rear Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Rear Commission: Rear Garrison, Henghai, Yingyang, Xingwu, and Jiangyin Guards.

sentences.zh: 又親軍衛指揮使司十有七：曰金吾前衛，曰金吾後衛，曰金吾左衛，曰金吾右衛，曰羽林左衛，曰羽林右衛，曰羽林前衛，曰府軍衛，曰府軍左衛，曰府軍右衛，曰府軍後衛，曰虎賁左衛，曰錦衣衛，曰旗手衛，曰江淮衛，曰濟州衛，曰孝陵衛。

translations.literal: Seventeen further personal guard commands: Forward, Rear, Left, and Right Golden Crow Guards; Left and Right Feathered Forest Guards; Forward Feathered Forest Guard; Military Household Guard and its Left, Right, and Rear branches; Left Tiger Guard; Embroidered Uniform Guard; Archery Guard; Jianghuai Guard; Jizhou Guard; and Xiaoling Mausoleum Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen personal guards: Golden Crow (forward, rear, left, right), Feathered Forest (left, right, forward), Military Household branches, Left Tiger, Embroidered Uniform, Archery, Jianghuai, Jizhou, and Xiaoling Mausoleum Guards.

sentences.zh: 與左府所屬十衛，右府所屬五衛，前府所屬七衛，後府所屬五衛，並聽中府節制。

translations.literal: Together with the ten guards of the Left Commission, five of the Right, seven of the Forward, and five of the Rear, all were subject to the Central Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Together with the Left Commission's ten, Right's five, Forward's seven, and Rear's five, all were under the Central Commission.

sentences.zh: 各衛領所一百一十有八。

translations.literal: The guards commanded one hundred eighteen battalions in all.
translations.idiomatic: All guards together commanded 118 battalions.

sentences.zh: 王府護衛指揮使司，設官如京衛。

translations.literal: Princely household guard commands were organized like capital guards.
translations.idiomatic: Princely household guard commands mirrored capital guards.

sentences.zh: 王府儀衛司。

translations.literal: Princely Ceremonial Guard Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Each princely establishment had a Ceremonial Guard Office.

sentences.zh: 儀衛正一人，正五品儀衛副二人，從五品典仗六人。

translations.literal: One ceremonial commissioner of the fifth rank; two vice commissioners of the fifth rank; six ritual staff officers of the sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: One fifth-rank ceremonial commissioner, two fifth-rank vice commissioners, and six sixth-rank ritual staff officers.

sentences.zh: 正六品儀衛，掌侍衛儀仗。

translations.literal: Ceremonial guards managed bodyguard regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial guards handled bodyguard regalia.

sentences.zh: 護衛，掌防禦非常，護衛王邸。

translations.literal: Household guards guarded against emergencies and protected the princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: Household guards defended against emergencies and protected the prince's residence.

sentences.zh: 有徵調，則聽命於朝。

translations.literal: When mobilized, they obeyed imperial orders.
translations.idiomatic: When called to campaign, they obeyed the court.

sentences.zh: 明初，諸王府置護軍府。

translations.literal: In early Ming all princely establishments had Military Protection Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Early Ming princely establishments had Military Protection Offices.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，置儀衛司，司設正、副各一人，秩比正、副千戶；

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu Ceremonial Guard Offices were established, each with one commissioner and one vice commissioner, ranks equal to chief and vice thousand-man chiefs;
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 3 Ceremonial Guard Offices were set up with commissioner and vice commissioner equal in rank to chief and vice thousand-man chiefs;

sentences.zh: 司仗六人，秩比百戶。

translations.literal: six ritual staff officers equal in rank to company officers.
translations.idiomatic: six ritual staff officers equal to company officers.

sentences.zh: 四年，改司仗為典仗。

translations.literal: In the fourth year ritual staff officers were renamed ritual bearers.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 ritual staff officers became ritual bearers.

sentences.zh: 五年，置親王護衛指揮使司，每王府設三護衛，衛設左、右、前、後、中五所，所千戶二人，百戶十人。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Princely Household Guard commands were established, three per princely establishment, each with left, right, forward, rear, and central battalions—two thousand-man chiefs and ten company officers per battalion.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 each prince received three household guard commands with five battalions each (left, right, forward, rear, central), two thousand-man chiefs and ten company officers per battalion.

sentences.zh: 又設圍子手二所，每所千戶一人。

translations.literal: Two Huntsmen battalions were also established, one thousand-man chief each.
translations.idiomatic: Two Huntsmen battalions were added, each with one thousand-man chief.

sentences.zh: 九年，罷護軍府。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Military Protection Offices were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 9 the Military Protection Offices were abolished.

sentences.zh: 建文中，改儀衛司為儀仗司，增置吏目一人。

translations.literal: Under Jianwen the Ceremonial Guard Office became the Ceremonial Regalia Office and one clerk was added.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianwen it became the Ceremonial Regalia Office with an added clerk.

sentences.zh: 成祖初復舊制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongle reign the old system was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle restored the former system.

sentences.zh: 總兵官、副總兵、參將、遊擊將軍、守備、把總，無品級，無定員。

translations.literal: Regional commander-in-chief, deputy commander-in-chief, deputy general, mobile commander, garrison commander, and company commander had no rank grades and no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commanders, deputy commanders, deputy generals, mobile commanders, garrison commanders, and company commanders had no rank and no fixed establishment.

sentences.zh: 總鎮一方者為鎮守，獨鎮一路者為分守，各守一城一堡者為守備，與主將同守一城者為協守。

translations.literal: One who guarded an entire region was a regional garrison commander; one who guarded a single route was a route garrison commander; those who each guarded a city or fort were garrison commanders; one who jointly guarded a city with the chief commander was a co-garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commanders guarded whole regions; route commanders guarded single routes; garrison commanders held cities or forts; co-garrison commanders shared a city with the chief.

sentences.zh: 又有提督、提調、巡視、備禦、領班、備倭等名。

translations.literal: Other titles included superintendent, coordinator, inspector, defense preparer, shift leader, and anti-Japanese defense commander.
translations.idiomatic: Other titles included superintendent, coordinator, inspector, defense preparer, shift leader, and anti-pirate commander.

sentences.zh: 凡總兵、副總兵，率以公、侯、伯、都督充之。

translations.literal: Regional and deputy commanders were usually filled by dukes, marquises, earls, and commanders-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Regional and deputy commanders were usually dukes, marquises, earls, or commanders-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 其總兵掛印稱將軍者，雲南曰徵南將軍，大同曰徵西前將軍，湖廣曰平蠻將軍，兩廣曰徵蠻將軍，遼東曰徵虜前將軍，宣府曰鎮朔將軍，甘肅曰平羌將軍，寧夏曰徵西將軍，交阯曰副將軍，延綏曰鎮西將軍。

translations.literal: Regional commanders bearing seals styled General included: Yunnan, Pacification South General; Datong, Forward Pacification West General; Huguang, Pacification of the Miao General; Liangguang, Pacification of the Miao General; Liaodong, Forward Subjugation of the Barbarians General; Xuanfu, Subjugation of the North General; Gansu, Pacification of the Qiang General; Ningxia, Pacification West General; Jiaozhi, Deputy General; Yan-sui, Pacification West General.
translations.idiomatic: Sealed generals included Pacification South (Yunnan), Forward Pacification West (Datong), Pacification of the Miao (Huguang and Liangguang), Forward Subjugation of Barbarians (Liaodong), Subjugation of the North (Xuanfu), Pacification of the Qiang (Gansu), Pacification West (Ningxia and Yan-sui), and Deputy General (Jiaozhi).

sentences.zh: 諸印，洪熙元年制頒。

translations.literal: These seals were issued in the first year of Hongxi.
translations.idiomatic: The seals were issued in Hongxi 1.

sentences.zh: 其在薊鎮、貴州、湖廣、四川及亻贊運淮安者，不得稱將軍掛印。

translations.literal: At Jizhen, Guizhou, Huguang, Sichuan, and grain transport at Huai'an, the title General with seal was not used.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhen, Guizhou, Huguang, Sichuan, and Huai'an grain transport could not use the sealed General title.

sentences.zh: 宣德間，又設山西、陝西二總兵。

translations.literal: In the Xuande reign regional commanders were also established for Shanxi and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xuande regional commanders were added for Shanxi and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖間，分設廣東、廣西、貴州、湖廣二總兵為四，改設福建、保定副總兵為總兵，又添設浙江總兵。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign Liangguang was split into Guangdong and Guangxi and Huguang into two; Fujian and Baoding deputy commanders became regional commanders; a Zhejiang regional commander was added.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiajing Liangguang split into Guangdong and Guangxi, Huguang into two, Fujian and Baoding deputies became regional commanders, and Zhejiang gained a regional commander.

sentences.zh: 萬曆間，又增設於臨洮、山海。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign posts were added at Lintao and Shanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli commanders were added at Lintao and Shanhai.

sentences.zh: 天啟間，增設登萊。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign Deng-Lai was added.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi Deng-Lai was added.

sentences.zh: 至崇禎時，益紛不可紀，而位權亦非復當日。

translations.literal: By the Chongzhen era appointments proliferated beyond record, and their standing was no longer what it had been.
translations.idiomatic: By Chongzhen posts multiplied beyond counting and their authority was no longer what it once was.

sentences.zh: 蓋明初，雖參將、遊擊、把總，亦多有充以勳戚都督等官，至後則杳然矣。

translations.literal: In early Ming even deputy generals, mobile commanders, and company commanders were often filled by meritorious kin and commanders-in-chief; later such appointments vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Early Ming even deputies and company commanders were often ennobled commanders; later that practice disappeared.

sentences.zh: 鎮守薊州總兵官一人，舊設。

translations.literal: One regional commander garrisoning Jizhou—an old establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhou had one regional commander—an old post.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年，改為總理練兵事務兼鎮守，駐三屯營。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longqing the title was changed to Superintendent of Drill with concurrent garrison command, stationed at Santun Camp.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 2 the post became superintendent of drill with garrison duty, based at Santun Camp.

sentences.zh: 協守副總兵三人。

translations.literal: Three co-garrison deputy commanders.
translations.idiomatic: There were three co-garrison deputy commanders.

sentences.zh: 東路副總兵，隆慶二年添設，駐建昌營，管理燕河營、臺頭營、石門寨、山海關四路。

translations.literal: Eastern-route deputy commander, added Longqing 2, stationed at Jianchang Camp, managing Yanhe, Taitou, Shimenzhai, and Shanhaiguan routes.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern-route deputy (Longqing 2) at Jianchang Camp over Yanhe, Taitou, Shimenzhai, and Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 中路副總兵，萬曆四年改設，駐三屯營，帶管馬蘭峪、鬆棚峪、喜峯口、太平寨四路。

translations.literal: Central-route deputy commander, changed Wanli 4, stationed at Santun Camp, overseeing Malanyu, Songpengyu, Xifengkou, and Taipingzhai routes.
translations.idiomatic: Central-route deputy (Wanli 4) at Santun Camp over Malanyu, Songpengyu, Xifengkou, and Taipingzhai.

sentences.zh: 西路副總兵，隆慶三年添設，駐石匣營，管理牆子嶺、曹家寨、古北口、石塘嶺四路。

translations.literal: Western-route deputy commander, added Longqing 3, stationed at Shixia Camp, managing Qiangziling, Caojiazhai, Gubeikou, and Shitangling routes.
translations.idiomatic: Western-route deputy (Longqing 3) at Shixia Camp over Qiangziling, Caojiazhai, Gubeikou, and Shitangling.

sentences.zh: 分守參將十一人，曰通州參將，曰山海關參將，曰石門寨參將，曰燕河營參將，曰石塘嶺參將，曰臺頭營參將，曰太平寨參將，曰馬蘭峪參將，曰牆子嶺參將，曰古北口參將，曰喜峯口參將。

translations.literal: Eleven route garrison deputy generals: Tongzhou, Shanhaiguan, Shimenzhai, Yanhe, Shitangling, Taitou, Taipingzhai, Malanyu, Qiangziling, Gubeikou, and Xifengkou.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven route deputies: Tongzhou, Shanhaiguan, Shimenzhai, Yanhe, Shitangling, Taitou, Taipingzhai, Malanyu, Qiangziling, Gubeikou, and Xifengkou.

sentences.zh: 遊擊將軍六人，統領南兵遊擊將軍三人，領班遊擊將軍七人，坐營官八人，守備八人，把總一人，提調官二十六人。

translations.literal: Six mobile commanders; three southern-troop mobile commanders; seven shift mobile commanders; eight camp officers; eight garrison commanders; one company commander; twenty-six coordinators.
translations.idiomatic: Six mobile commanders, three southern-troop mobile commanders, seven shift mobile commanders, eight camp officers, eight garrison commanders, one company commander, and twenty-six coordinators.

sentences.zh: 鎮守昌平總兵官一人，舊設副總兵，又有提督武臣。

translations.literal: One regional commander garrisoning Changping—an old establishment with deputy commander and a supervising military minister.
translations.idiomatic: One Changping regional commander (old post) with deputy and supervising military minister.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十八年，裁副總兵，以提督改為鎮守總兵，駐昌平城，聽總督節制。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Jiajing the deputy was cut; the supervisor became regional commander at Changping city under the governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 38 the deputy was abolished and the supervisor became regional commander at Changping under the governor-general.

sentences.zh: 分守參將三人，曰居庸關參將，曰黃花鎮參將，曰橫嶺口參將。

translations.literal: Three route garrison deputy generals: Juyongguan, Huanghuazhen, and Henglingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Three route deputies: Juyongguan, Huanghuazhen, and Henglingkou.

sentences.zh: 遊擊將軍二人，坐營官三人，守備十人，提調官一人。

translations.literal: Two mobile commanders; three camp officers; ten garrison commanders; one coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: Two mobile commanders, three camp officers, ten garrison commanders, and one coordinator.

sentences.zh: 鎮守遼東總兵官一人，舊設，駐廣寧。

translations.literal: One regional commander garrisoning Liaodong—old establishment, stationed at Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: One Liaodong regional commander (old post) at Guangning.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年，令冬月移駐河東遼陽適中之地，調度防禦，應援海州、瀋陽。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing he was ordered to move in winter to a central place east of the Liao River at Liaoyang to direct defense and support Haizhou and Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 1 he wintered at Liaoyang east of the Liao to direct defense and support Haizhou and Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 協守副總兵一人，遼陽副總兵舊為分守，嘉靖四十五年改為協守，駐遼陽城，節制開原、海州、險山、瀋陽等處。

translations.literal: One co-garrison deputy commander; the Liaoyang deputy was formerly route garrison commander, changed Jiajing 45 to co-garrison deputy at Liaoyang city, overseeing Kaifeng, Haizhou, Xianshan, Shenyang, and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: One co-garrison deputy; Liaoyang deputy (formerly route commander, Jiajing 45) at Liaoyang over Kaifeng, Haizhou, Xianshan, and Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 分守參將五人。

translations.literal: Five route garrison deputy generals.
translations.idiomatic: Five route garrison deputy generals were appointed.

sentences.zh: 曰開原參將，曰錦義右參將，曰海蓋右參將，曰寧遠參將，曰寬奠堡參將。

translations.literal: Kaifeng, Right Jin-Yi, Right Hai-Gai, Ningyuan, and Kuandian Fort deputy generals.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng; Right Jin-Yi; Right Hai-Gai; Ningyuan; and Kuandian Fort deputies.

sentences.zh: 遊擊將軍八人，守備五人，坐營中軍官一人，備禦十九人。

translations.literal: Eight mobile commanders; five garrison commanders; one camp staff officer; nineteen defense preparers.
translations.idiomatic: Eight mobile commanders, five garrison commanders, one camp staff officer, and nineteen defense preparers.

sentences.zh: 鎮守保定總兵官一人。

translations.literal: One regional commander garrisoning Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: Baoding had one regional commander.

sentences.zh: 弘治十八年，初設保定副總兵，後改為參將。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Hongzhi a Baoding deputy commander was first established, later changed to deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 18 first created a Baoding deputy, later a deputy general.

sentences.zh: 正德九年，復為分守副總兵。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhengde it again became route garrison deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 9 restored route garrison deputy.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十年，改為鎮守。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Jiajing it became regional garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 20 made it regional garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 三十年，改設鎮守總兵官。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year the regional commander-in-chief post was established.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 30 established the regional commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 萬曆元年，令春秋兩防移駐浮圖峪，遇有警，移駐紫荊關，以備入援。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wanli he was ordered to move each spring and autumn to Futuyu; on alarm he moved to Zijingguan to prepare relief.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 1 ordered spring and autumn stationing at Futuyu and move to Zijingguan on alarm for relief.

sentences.zh: 分守參將四人，曰紫荊關參將，曰龍固二關參將，曰馬水口參將，曰倒馬關參將。

translations.literal: Four route garrison deputy generals: Zijingguan, Longgu Passes, Mashuikou, and Daomaguan.
translations.idiomatic: Four route deputies: Zijingguan, Longgu Passes, Mashuikou, and Daomaguan.

sentences.zh: 遊擊將軍六人，坐營中軍官一人，守備七人，把總七人，忠順官二人。

translations.literal: Six mobile commanders; one camp staff officer; seven garrison commanders; seven company commanders; two Zhongshun officials.
translations.idiomatic: Six mobile commanders, one camp staff officer, seven garrison commanders, seven company commanders, and two Zhongshun officials.

sentences.zh: 鎮守宣府總兵官一人，舊設，駐宣府鎮城。

translations.literal: One regional commander garrisoning Xuanfu—old establishment at Xuanfu town.
translations.idiomatic: One Xuanfu regional commander (old post) at Xuanfu town.

sentences.zh: 協守副總兵一人，副總兵舊亦駐鎮城，嘉靖二十八年移駐永寧城。

translations.literal: One co-garrison deputy commander, formerly also at the town; in the twenty-eighth year of Jiajing moved to Yongning city.
translations.idiomatic: One co-garrison deputy (formerly at town, Jiajing 28 at Yongning).

sentences.zh: 分守參將七人，曰北路獨石馬營參將，曰東路懷來永寧參將，曰上西路萬全右衛參將，曰南路順聖蔚廣參將，曰中路葛峪堡參將，曰下西路柴溝堡參將，曰南山參將。

translations.literal: Seven route garrison deputy generals: North Route Dushi-Maying; East Route Huailai-Yongning; Upper West Wanquan Right Guard; South Route Shun-Sheng-Wei-Guang; Central Geyubao; Lower West Chaigoubao; South Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Seven route deputies: North Dushi-Maying; East Huailai-Yongning; Upper West Wanquan Right; South Shun-Sheng-Wei-Guang; Central Geyubao; Lower West Chaigoubao; South Mountain.

sentences.zh: 遊擊將軍三人，坐營中軍官二人，守備三十一人，領班備禦二人。

translations.literal: Three mobile commanders; two camp staff officers; thirty-one garrison commanders; two shift defense preparers.
translations.idiomatic: Three mobile commanders, two camp staff officers, thirty-one garrison commanders, and two shift defense preparers.

sentences.zh: 萬曆八年革。

translations.literal: Abolished in the eighth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Abolished in Wanli 8.

sentences.zh: 鎮守大同總兵官一人，舊設，駐大同鎮城。

translations.literal: One regional commander garrisoning Datong—old establishment at Datong town.
translations.idiomatic: One Datong regional commander (old post) at Datong town.

sentences.zh: 協守副總兵一人，舊為左副總兵，萬曆五年去左字，駐左衛城。

translations.literal: One co-garrison deputy commander, formerly left deputy commander; in Wanli 5 the word "left" was dropped; stationed at Left Guard city.
translations.idiomatic: One co-garrison deputy (formerly left deputy, Wanli 5 without "left") at Left Guard city.

sentences.zh: 分守參將九人，曰東路參將，曰北東路參將，曰中路參將，曰西路參將，曰北西路參將，曰井坪城參將，曰新坪堡參將，曰總督標下左掖參將，曰威遠城參將，萬曆八年革。

translations.literal: Nine route garrison deputy generals: East, North-East, Central, West, North-West, Jingping, Xinpingbao, Governor's Left Flank, and Weiyuan—abolished Wanli 8.
translations.idiomatic: Nine route deputies (East, North-East, Central, West, North-West, Jingping, Xinpingbao, Governor's Left Flank, Weiyuan)—abolished Wanli 8.

sentences.zh: 遊擊將軍二人，入衛遊擊四人，坐營中軍官二人，守備三十九人。

translations.literal: Two mobile commanders; four palace-entry mobile commanders; two camp staff officers; thirty-nine garrison commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Two mobile commanders, four palace-entry mobile commanders, two camp staff officers, and thirty-nine garrison commanders.
