translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the Central Capital Garrison Command was first established, overseeing eight guards: Fengyang, Central Fengyang, Right Fengyang, Imperial Mausoleum, Left Garrison, Central Garrison, Changhuai, and Huaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 14 created the Central Capital Garrison Command over eight guards: Fengyang, Central Fengyang, Right Fengyang, Imperial Mausoleum, Left Garrison, Central Garrison, Changhuai, and Huaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 防護皇陵，設留守一人，左、右副留守各一人。

translations.literal: To protect the imperial mausoleum, one chief garrison commander and left and right vice commanders were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: For imperial mausoleum protection: one chief commander and left and right vice commanders.

sentences.zh: 屬官經歷以下，如前所列。

translations.literal: Subordinate officials from registrar downward were as listed above.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates from registrar down were as listed above.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十八年，改荊州左衛為顯陵衛，置興都留守司，統顯陵、承天二衛，防護顯陵，設官如中都焉。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Jiajing Jingzhou Left Guard became Xianling Guard and the Xingdu Garrison Command was established, overseeing Xianling and Chengtian guards to protect the Xian mausoleum, with officials as at Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 18 made Jingzhou Left Guard into Xianling Guard and created the Xingdu Garrison Command over Xianling and Chengtian guards, organized like Zhongdu.

sentences.zh: 都指揮使司。

translations.literal: Regional Military Commissions.
translations.idiomatic: The Regional Military Commissions.

sentences.zh: 都指揮使一人，正二品都指揮同知二人，從二品都指揮僉事四人。

translations.literal: One regional commander of the second rank; two vice regional commanders of the third rank; four assistant regional commanders of the fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: One second-rank regional commander, two third-rank vice commanders, and four fourth-rank assistants.

sentences.zh: 正三品其屬，經歷司，經歷，正六品都事。

translations.literal: Subordinates: Registry with registrar of the sixth rank and secretary of the seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates: Registry with sixth-rank registrar and seventh-rank secretary.

sentences.zh: 正七品斷事司，斷事，正六品副斷事，正七品吏目各一人。

translations.literal: Judicial Office with judge of the sixth rank, vice judge of the seventh rank, and clerk—one each.
translations.idiomatic: Judicial Office with sixth-rank judge, seventh-rank vice judge, and one clerk.

sentences.zh: 司獄司，司獄。

translations.literal: Prison Office with prison keeper of the ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: A Prison Office with a ninth-rank keeper.

sentences.zh: 從九品倉庫、草場，大使、副使各一人。

translations.literal: Granary and fodder grounds with commissioner and deputy of the ninth rank—one each.
translations.idiomatic: Granary and fodder grounds with ninth-rank commissioner and deputy each.

sentences.zh: 行都指揮使司，設官與都指揮使司同。

translations.literal: Traveling regional military commissions had the same offices as regional commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling regional commissions had the same organization as regular commissions.

sentences.zh: 都司，掌一方之軍政，各率其衛所以隸於五府，而聽於兵部。

translations.literal: Regional commissions directed military affairs in a region, each leading its guards and battalions subordinate to the five commissions and answering to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commissions ran military affairs in their area, leading guards and battalions under the five commissions and the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 凡都司並流官，或得世官，歲撫、按察其賢否，五歲考選軍政而廢置之。

translations.literal: For regional commissions and appointive posts, or hereditary posts where permitted, the provincial governor and surveillance commissioner annually inspected merit and every five years military administration was examined for promotion or removal.
translations.idiomatic: Appointive and permitted hereditary posts were inspected yearly by provincial governors and surveillance commissioners; military administration was reviewed every five years.

sentences.zh: 都指揮使及同知僉事，常以一人統司事，曰掌印，一人練兵，一人屯田，曰僉書。

translations.literal: Regional commander and vice and assistant commanders usually had one directing commission affairs as seal-holder, one drilling troops, and one garrison farming as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Usually one directed as seal-holder, one drilled troops, and one managed garrison farming as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 巡捕、軍器、漕運、京操、備禦諸雜務，並選充之，否則曰帶俸。

translations.literal: Patrol, ordnance, grain transport, capital drill, and defense duties were filled by selection; otherwise they drew stipends only.
translations.idiomatic: Patrol, ordnance, transport, capital drill, and defense posts were filled by selection; otherwise officers were stipend-only.

sentences.zh: 凡備倭守備行都指揮事者，不得建牙、升公座。

translations.literal: Those serving anti-Japanese garrison duty as traveling regional commanders might not erect staffs or occupy the high seat.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling regional commanders on anti-pirate garrison duty could not erect staffs or take the high seat.

sentences.zh: 凡朝廷吉凶表箋，序銜布、按二司上。

translations.literal: For court felicitations and memorials, they ranked after the provincial administration and surveillance commissions.
translations.idiomatic: In court documents they ranked after provincial administration and surveillance commissions.

sentences.zh: 經歷、都事，典文移。

translations.literal: Registrars and secretaries managed documents.
translations.idiomatic: Registrars and secretaries handled documents.

sentences.zh: 斷事，理刑獄。

translations.literal: Judges handled criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: Judges tried criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 明初，置各行省行都督府，設官如都督府。

translations.literal: In early Ming traveling provincial military commissions were established with offices like the chief military commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Early Ming created traveling provincial military commissions modeled on the chief commissions.

sentences.zh: 又置各都衛指揮使司。

translations.literal: Regional guard commands were also established.
translations.idiomatic: Regional guard commands were also created.

sentences.zh: 洪武四年，置各都衛斷事司，以理軍官、軍人詞訟。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongwu judicial offices were added to regional guards to handle lawsuits of officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 4 added judicial offices to regional guards for officer and soldier lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 又以都衛節制方面，職系甚重，從朝廷選擇升調，不許世襲。

translations.literal: Because regional guards controlled whole regions and their duties were weighty, appointments were chosen and transferred by the court and were not hereditary.
translations.idiomatic: Because regional guards controlled whole regions, appointments came from the court and were not hereditary.

sentences.zh: 七年，置西安行都衛指揮使司於河州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Xi'an Traveling Regional Guard Command was established at Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 7 established the Xi'an traveling regional guard command at Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 八年十月，詔各都衛並改為都指揮使司，凡改設都司十有三，燕山都衛為北平都司，西安都衛為陝西都司，太原都衛為山西都司，杭州都衛為浙江都司，江西都衛為江西都司，青州都衛為山東都司，成都都衛為四川都司，福州都衛為福建都司，武昌都衛為湖廣都司，廣東都衛為廣東都司。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the eighth year an edict changed all regional guards to regional military commissions; thirteen were re-established: Yanshan Guard became Beiping Commission, Xi'an Guard became Shaanxi Commission, Taiyuan became Shanxi, Hangzhou Zhejiang, Jiangxi Jiangxi, Qingzhou Shandong, Chengdu Sichuan, Fuzhou Fujian, Wuchang Huguang, Guangdong Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 8 month 10 changed all regional guards to commissions—thirteen conversions including Yanshan to Beiping, Xi'an to Shaanxi, Taiyuan to Shanxi, Hangzhou to Zhejiang, and others listed.

sentences.zh: 廣西都衛為廣西都司，定遼都衛為遼東都司，河南都衛為河南都司。

translations.literal: Guangxi Guard became Guangxi Commission, Dingliao became Liaodong, Henan Guard became Henan Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi, Dingliao, and Henan guards became Guangxi, Liaodong, and Henan commissions.

sentences.zh: 行都司三，西安行都衛為陝西行都司，大同都衛為山西行都司，建甯都衛為福建行都司。

translations.literal: Three traveling commissions: Xi'an traveling guard became Shaanxi Traveling Commission, Datong became Shanxi Traveling Commission, Jianning became Fujian Traveling Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Three traveling commissions: Xi'an to Shaanxi Traveling, Datong to Shanxi Traveling, Jianning to Fujian Traveling.

sentences.zh: 十五年，增置貴州、雲南二都司。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Guizhou and Yunnan commissions were added.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 15 added Guizhou and Yunnan commissions.

sentences.zh: 後以北平都司為北平行都司。

translations.literal: Later Beiping Commission became Beiping Traveling Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Later Beiping became a traveling commission.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年改為大寧都司。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle it became Daning Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle 1 made it Daning Commission.

sentences.zh: 宣德中，增置萬全都司。

translations.literal: In the Xuande reign Wanquan Commission was added.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xuande Wanquan Commission was added.

sentences.zh: 計天下都司凡十有六。

translations.literal: Regional commissions nationwide totaled sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: There were sixteen regional commissions nationwide.

sentences.zh: 十三省都司外，有遼東、大寧、萬全三都司。

translations.literal: Besides the thirteen provinces, there were Liaodong, Daning, and Wanquan commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the thirteen provinces were Liaodong, Daning, and Wanquan.

sentences.zh: 又於建昌置四川行都司，於鄖陽置湖廣行都司。

translations.literal: A Sichuan Traveling Commission was also placed at Jianchang and a Huguang Traveling Commission at Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan Traveling Commission was at Jianchang and Huguang Traveling at Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 計天下行都司凡五。

translations.literal: Traveling commissions nationwide totaled five.
translations.idiomatic: There were five traveling commissions nationwide.

sentences.zh: 明初，又於各行省置都鎮撫司，設都鎮撫，從四品副鎮撫，從五品知事。

translations.literal: In early Ming Military Pacification Commissions were also placed in each province with pacification commissioner of the fourth rank, vice pacifier of the fifth rank, and secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Early Ming also placed Military Pacification Commissions in each province with fourth-rank commissioner, fifth-rank vice commissioner, and secretary.

sentences.zh: 從八品吳元年改都鎮撫正五品，副鎮撫正六品，知事為提控案牘，省注。

translations.literal: of the eighth rank. In the first year of the Wu reign era pacification commissioners were raised to the fifth rank, vice pacifiers to the sixth, and secretaries became records controllers per abbreviated regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth rank. In Wu year 1 commissioners became fifth rank, vice commissioners sixth, and secretaries records controllers under abbreviated rules.

sentences.zh: 洪武六年罷。

translations.literal: Abolished in the sixth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: It was abolished in Hongwu 6.

sentences.zh: 衛指揮使司，設官如京衛。

translations.literal: Guard commands were organized like capital guards.
translations.idiomatic: Guard commands followed the same organization as capital guards.

sentences.zh: 品秩並同外衛各統於都司、行都司或留守司。

translations.literal: Ranks were the same as outer guards; each was subordinate to a regional commission, traveling regional commission, or garrison command.
translations.idiomatic: Ranks matched outer guards; each reported to a regional, traveling regional, or garrison command.

sentences.zh: 率世官，或有流官。

translations.literal: They were hereditary in the main, though some posts were appointive.
translations.idiomatic: Posts were mostly hereditary, with some appointive exceptions.

sentences.zh: 凡襲替、升授、優給、優養及屬所軍政，掌印、僉事報都指揮使司，達所隸都督府，移兵部。

translations.literal: For succession, promotion, preferential grants and maintenance, and battalion military administration, the seal-holder and chief secretary reported to the regional commission, which forwarded to the supervising commission and the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Succession, promotion, grants, maintenance, and battalion affairs went from seal-holder and chief secretary to the regional commission, then the supervising commission and Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 每歲撫、按察其賢否，五歲一考選軍政，廢置之。

translations.literal: Each year the governor and surveillance commissioner inspected merit; every five years military administration was examined for promotion or removal.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial governors and surveillance commissioners inspected them yearly; military administration was reviewed every five years.

sentences.zh: 凡管理衛事，惟屬掌印、僉書。

translations.literal: Management of guard affairs belonged solely to the seal-holder and chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Only the seal-holder and chief secretary managed guard affairs.

sentences.zh: 不論指揮使、同知、僉事，考選其才者充之。

translations.literal: Regardless of commander, vice commander, or assistant commander, those selected for ability filled the posts.
translations.idiomatic: Commander, vice commander, or assistant—whoever was chosen for ability held the post.

sentences.zh: 分理屯田、驗軍、營操、巡捕、漕運、備禦、出哨、入衛、戍守、軍器諸雜務，曰見任管事；

translations.literal: Dividing garrison farming, troop inspection, camp drill, patrol, grain transport, defense preparation, outbound patrol, palace entry, garrison duty, and ordnance and other duties was called serving in active management;
translations.idiomatic: Active duties—garrison farming, inspection, drill, patrol, transport, defense, outbound patrol, palace entry, garrison duty, and ordnance—were called serving in management;

sentences.zh: 不任事入隊，曰帶俸差操。

translations.literal: not holding office but entering the ranks was called drawing stipends with assigned drill.
translations.idiomatic: Officers without posts who only drilled were called stipend-only with assigned drill.

sentences.zh: 徵行，則率其屬，聽所命主帥調度。

translations.literal: On campaign they led their subordinates under the orders of the commander appointed over them.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign they led subordinates under their assigned commander.

sentences.zh: 所，千戶所，正千戶一人，正五品副千戶二人，從五品，鎮撫二人，從六品其屬，吏目一人。

translations.literal: Battalions: a thousand-man battalion had one chief thousand-man chief of the fifth rank, two vice chiefs of the fifth rank, two pacifiers of the sixth rank; subordinates included one clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Thousand-man battalions: one fifth-rank chief, two fifth-rank vice chiefs, two sixth-rank pacifiers, and one clerk.

sentences.zh: 所轄百戶所凡十，共百戶十人，正六品。

translations.literal: Under them were ten company offices with ten company officers of the sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: They commanded ten company offices with ten sixth-rank company officers.

sentences.zh: 升授、改調、增置無定員。

translations.literal: Promotion, transfer, and additions had no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Promotion, transfer, and new establishments had no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 總旗二十人，小旗百人。

translations.literal: Twenty platoon leaders and one hundred squad leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Each battalion had twenty platoon leaders and one hundred squad leaders.

sentences.zh: 其守禦千戶所，軍民千戶所設官並同。

translations.literal: Garrison-defense and military-civilian thousand-man battalions had the same offices.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison-defense and military-civilian battalions used the same offices.

sentences.zh: 凡千戶，一人掌印，一人僉書，曰管軍。

translations.literal: For each thousand-man battalion one held the seal and one was chief secretary, called troop managers.
translations.idiomatic: Each battalion had one seal-holder and one chief secretary who managed troops.

sentences.zh: 千戶、百戶，有試，有實授。

translations.literal: Thousand-man and company chiefs might be probationary or fully appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Thousand-man and company chiefs could be probationary or fully appointed.

sentences.zh: 其掌印，恆以一人兼數印。

translations.literal: The seal-holder often held several seals at once.
translations.idiomatic: One seal-holder often held multiple seals.

sentences.zh: 凡軍政，衛下於所，千戶督百戶，百戶下總旗、小旗，率其卒伍以聽令。

translations.literal: For military administration the guard reported down to battalions; thousand-man chiefs supervised company officers; company officers commanded platoon and squad leaders, who led soldiers to obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: Military administration ran guard to battalion; thousand-man chiefs over company officers; company officers over platoon and squad leaders who led soldiers.

sentences.zh: 鎮撫無獄事，則管軍，百戶缺，則代之。

translations.literal: If the pacifier had no prison duties, he managed troops; if a company officer was vacant, he acted in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Without prison duties the pacifier managed troops; if a company post was vacant he filled it.

sentences.zh: 其守禦千戶所，不隸衛，而自達於都司。

translations.literal: Garrison-defense thousand-man battalions were not subordinate to guards but reported directly to the regional commission.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison-defense battalions reported directly to the regional commission, not to guards.

sentences.zh: 凡衛所皆隸都司，而都司又分隸五軍都督府。

translations.literal: All guards and battalions were subordinate to regional commissions, and regional commissions in turn to the five chief military commissions.
translations.idiomatic: All guards and battalions reported to regional commissions, which reported to the five chief commissions.

sentences.zh: 浙江都司、山東都司、遼東都司，隸左軍都督府。

translations.literal: Zhejiang, Shandong, and Liaodong regional commissions were subordinate to the Left Army Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang, Shandong, and Liaodong commissions were under the Left Army Commission.

sentences.zh: 陝西都司、陝西行都司、四川都司、四川行都司、廣西都司、雲南都司、貴州都司，隸右軍都督府。

translations.literal: Shaanxi, Shaanxi Traveling, Sichuan, Sichuan Traveling, Guangxi, Yunnan, and Guizhou commissions were subordinate to the Right Army Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi, Shaanxi Traveling, Sichuan, Sichuan Traveling, Guangxi, Yunnan, and Guizhou were under the Right Army Commission.

sentences.zh: 中都留守司、河南都司，隸中軍都督府。

translations.literal: Central Capital Garrison Command and Henan Commission were subordinate to the Central Army Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongdu Garrison Command and Henan Commission were under the Central Army Commission.

sentences.zh: 興都留守司、湖廣都司、湖廣行都司、福建都司、福建行都司、江西都司、廣東都司，隸前軍都督府。

translations.literal: Xingdu Garrison Command, Huguang, Huguang Traveling, Fujian, Fujian Traveling, Jiangxi, and Guangdong commissions were subordinate to the Forward Army Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Xingdu Garrison, Huguang, Huguang Traveling, Fujian, Fujian Traveling, Jiangxi, and Guangdong were under the Forward Army Commission.

sentences.zh: 大寧都司、萬全都司、山西都司、山西行都司，隸後軍都督府。

translations.literal: Daning, Wanquan, Shanxi, and Shanxi Traveling commissions were subordinate to the Rear Army Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Daning, Wanquan, Shanxi, and Shanxi Traveling were under the Rear Army Commission.

sentences.zh: 明初，置千戶所，設正千戶，正五品副千戶，從五品鎮撫、百戶。

translations.literal: In early Ming thousand-man battalions were established with chief thousand-man chief of the fifth rank, vice chief of the fifth rank, pacifier, and company officer of the sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Early Ming created thousand-man battalions with fifth-rank chiefs and vice chiefs, pacifiers, and sixth-rank company officers.

sentences.zh: 正六品又立各萬戶府，設正萬戶，正四品副萬戶，從四品知事，從八品照磨。

translations.literal: Ten-thousand-man offices were also established with chief ten-thousand-man chief of the fourth rank, vice chief of the fourth rank, secretary of the eighth rank, and registrar-clerk of the ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Ten-thousand-man offices were added with fourth-rank chiefs and vice chiefs, eighth-rank secretaries, and ninth-rank registrar-clerks.

sentences.zh: 正九品尋以名不稱實，遂罷萬戶府，而設指揮使及千戶等官。

translations.literal: Soon because the name did not match reality the ten-thousand-man offices were abolished and commanders and thousand-man chiefs were established instead.
translations.idiomatic: Because the title did not match reality, ten-thousand-man offices were abolished in favor of commanders and thousand-man chiefs.

sentences.zh: 核諸將所部有兵五千者為指揮使，千人者為千戶，百人者為百戶，五十人為總旗，十人為小旗。

translations.literal: Forces under each general were graded: five thousand men made a command, one thousand a thousand-man battalion, one hundred a company, fifty a platoon, and ten a squad.
translations.idiomatic: Forces were graded by size: 5,000 men to a command, 1,000 to a battalion, 100 to a company, 50 to a platoon, 10 to a squad.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年，置刻期百戶所，選能疾行者二百人，以百戶領之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongwu timed company offices were established, choosing two hundred men able to march swiftly, led by a company officer.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 2 created timed company offices of two hundred swift marchers under a company officer.

sentences.zh: 七年，申定衛所之制。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the guard and battalion system was formally fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 7 fixed the guard and battalion system.

sentences.zh: 先是，內外衛所，凡一衛統十千戶，一千戶統十百戶，百戶領總旗二，總旗領小旗五，小旗領軍十。

translations.literal: Previously, inner and outer guards each had one guard commanding ten thousand-man battalions, each battalion ten companies, each company two platoon leaders, each platoon five squad leaders, each squad ten soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Previously one guard had ten battalions, each battalion ten companies, each company two platoon leaders, each platoon five squads of ten soldiers.

sentences.zh: 至是更定其制，每衛設前、後、中、左、右五千戶所，大率以五千六百人為一衛，一千一百二十人為一千戶所，一百一十二人為一百戶所，每百戶所設總旗二人，小旗十人。

translations.literal: Now the system was revised: each guard had forward, rear, central, left, and right battalions; roughly five thousand six hundred men per guard, one thousand one hundred twenty per battalion, one hundred twelve per company, with two platoon leaders and ten squad leaders per company.
translations.idiomatic: The revision gave each guard five battalions (forward, rear, central, left, right): about 5,600 men per guard, 1,120 per battalion, 112 per company, with two platoon leaders and ten squad leaders per company.

sentences.zh: 二十年，始命各衛立掌印、僉書，專職理事，以指揮使掌印，同知、僉事各領一所。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year each guard was ordered to appoint seal-holder and chief secretary dedicated to administration; the commander held the seal, vice commander and assistant each led one battalion.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 20 required dedicated seal-holder and chief secretary; the commander held the seal while vice and assistant each led a battalion.

sentences.zh: 士卒有武藝不嫻、器械不利者，皆責所領之官。

translations.literal: Officers whose soldiers lacked martial skill or whose weapons were defective were all held responsible by the battalion officers under them.
translations.idiomatic: Battalion officers were responsible if soldiers lacked skill or weapons were defective.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，又設軍民指揮使司、軍民千戶所，計天下內外衛凡五百四十有七，所凡二千五百九十有三。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year Military-Civilian commands and Military-Civilian battalions were also established; guards nationwide totaled five hundred forty-seven and battalions two thousand five hundred ninety-three.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 23 added Military-Civilian commands and battalions; there were 547 guards and 2,593 battalions nationwide.

sentences.zh: 自衛指揮以下其官多世襲，其軍士亦父子相繼，為一代定制。

translations.literal: From guard commander down most offices were hereditary and soldiers also succeeded father to son—a system fixed for the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: From guard commander down offices were mostly hereditary and soldiers succeeded father to son—a dynastic norm.

sentences.zh: 土官，宣慰使司，宣慰使一人，從三品同知一人，正四品副使一人，從四品僉事一人。

translations.literal: Native officials: Pacification Commissions had one pacification commissioner of the third rank, one vice commissioner of the fourth rank, one deputy of the fourth rank, and one assistant of the fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissions: third-rank commissioner, fourth-rank vice and deputy, fifth-rank assistant.

sentences.zh: 正五品經歷司，經歷一人，從七品都事一人。

translations.literal: Registry with one registrar of the seventh rank and one secretary of the eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: A Registry with seventh-rank registrar and eighth-rank secretary.

sentences.zh: 正八品

translations.literal: of the eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: The secretary was eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 宣撫司，宣撫使一人，從四品同知一人，正五品副使一人，從五品僉事一人。

translations.literal: Pacification Superintendent Commissions had one superintendent of the fourth rank, one vice superintendent of the fifth rank, one deputy of the fifth rank, and one assistant of the sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Superintendent Commissions: fourth-rank superintendent, fifth-rank vice and deputy, sixth-rank assistant.

sentences.zh: 正六品經歷司，經歷一人，從八品知事一人，正九品照磨一人。

translations.literal: Registry with one registrar of the eighth rank, one secretary of the ninth rank, and one registrar-clerk of the ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Registry with eighth-rank registrar, ninth-rank secretary, and ninth-rank registrar-clerk.

sentences.zh: 從九品

translations.literal: of the ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: The registrar-clerk was ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 安撫司，安撫使一人，從五品同知一人，正六品副使一人，從六品僉事一人。

translations.literal: Comforting Commissions had one comforting commissioner of the fifth rank, one vice commissioner of the sixth rank, one deputy of the sixth rank, and one assistant of the seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Comforting Commissions: fifth-rank commissioner, sixth-rank vice and deputy, seventh-rank assistant.

sentences.zh: 正七品其屬，吏目一人。

translations.literal: Subordinates: one clerk of the ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates: one ninth-rank clerk.

sentences.zh: 從九品

translations.literal: of the ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk was ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 招討司，招討使一人，從五品副招討一人。

translations.literal: Pacification and Suppression Commissions had one pacification commissioner of the fifth rank and one vice pacification commissioner of the sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification and Suppression Commissions: fifth-rank commissioner and sixth-rank vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 正六品其屬，吏目一人。

translations.literal: Subordinates: one clerk of the ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates: one ninth-rank clerk.

sentences.zh: 從九品

translations.literal: of the ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk was ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 長官司，長官一人，正六品副長官一人，從七品其屬，吏目一人。

translations.literal: Native Official posts had one chief of the sixth rank and one vice chief of the seventh rank; subordinates: one clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Native Official posts: sixth-rank chief, seventh-rank vice chief, and one clerk.

sentences.zh: 未入流蠻夷長官司，長官、副長官各一人。

translations.literal: Barbarian Native Official posts had one chief and one vice chief each, of the same ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian Native Official posts had chief and vice chief of the same ranks.

sentences.zh: 品同上又有蠻夷官、苗民官及千夫長、副千夫長等官。

translations.literal: There were also barbarian officials, Miao officials, thousand-man chiefs, vice thousand-man chiefs, and similar posts.
translations.idiomatic: Additional posts included barbarian officials, Miao officials, thousand-man chiefs, and vice thousand-man chiefs.

sentences.zh: 軍民府、土州、土縣，設官如府州縣。

translations.literal: Military-Civilian prefectures and native prefectures and counties had offices like regular prefectures, departments, and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Military-Civilian prefectures and native prefectures and counties mirrored regular local government offices.

sentences.zh: 洪武七年，西南諸蠻夷朝貢，多因元官授之，稍與約束，定徵徭差發之法。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Hongwu southwestern tribes presented tribute; many were reappointed from Yuan offices, gradually brought under constraint, and rules for levies and corvée were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 7 southwestern tribes presented tribute; many kept Yuan appointments under new levy and corvée rules.

sentences.zh: 漸為宣慰司者十一，為招討司者一，為宣撫司者十，為安撫司者十九，為長官司者百七十有三。

translations.literal: Gradually there were eleven pacification commissions, one pacification and suppression commission, ten pacification superintendent commissions, nineteen comforting commissions, and one hundred seventy-three native official posts.
translations.idiomatic: Over time there were 11 pacification commissions, 1 pacification and suppression commission, 10 superintendent commissions, 19 comforting commissions, and 173 native official posts.

sentences.zh: 其府州縣正貳屬官，或土或流，大率宣慰等司經歷皆流官，府州縣佐貳多流官。

translations.literal: For prefectures, departments, and counties the chief and deputy posts might be native or appointive; generally pacification commission registrars were appointive and prefectural deputies mostly appointive.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural chiefs and deputies could be native or appointive; pacification registrars were usually appointive, prefectural deputies mostly appointive.

sentences.zh: 皆因其俗，使之附輯諸蠻，謹守疆土，修職貢，供徵調，無相攜貳。

translations.literal: According to local custom they were made to bring the tribes together, guard the frontier, maintain tribute, and supply levies without disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: By local custom they gathered tribes, guarded frontiers, maintained tribute, and supplied levies without disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 有相仇者，疏上聽命於天子。

translations.literal: If tribes feuded, they memorialized and awaited the Son of Heaven's command.
translations.idiomatic: Inter-tribal feuds were reported to await the emperor's order.

sentences.zh: 又有番夷都指揮使司三，衛指揮使司三百八十五，宣慰司三，招討司六，萬戶府四，千戶所四十一，站七，地面七，寨一，詳見《兵志·衛所》中。

translations.literal: There were also three frontier tribal regional commands, three hundred eighty-five guard commands, three pacification commissions, six pacification and suppression commissions, four ten-thousand-man offices, forty-one thousand-man battalions, seven relay stations, seven territories, and one stockade—as detailed in the Treatise on Military Affairs under Guards and Battalions.
translations.idiomatic: There were also three frontier tribal regional commands, 385 guard commands, 3 pacification commissions, 6 pacification and suppression commissions, 4 ten-thousand-man offices, 41 battalions, 7 relay stations, 7 territories, and 1 stockade—see the Treatise on Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 並以附寨番夷官其地。

translations.literal: Native officials were also appointed over those territories.
translations.idiomatic: Native officials were appointed over those territories as well.
